Thanks for the report! This looks like an enhancement request rather than a regression: the interactive "Issue type" prompt added in https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/0d121e8c31204cdbe02b4a4b1be5e88bdc3c4662/pkg/cmd/issue/create/create.go#L362-L378 always builds its option list directly from the repo's configured issue types and never inserts a "none selected" choice, so there's currently no way to skip setting a type interactively. I'm suggesting `enhancement` and `gh-issue`. This isn't a duplicate of #13804/#14367 (those are about the permission error thrown when applying the selected type), since this issue is specifically about the prompt lacking a "none" option.

Hey @A4-Tacks, is your issue here that you are being forced to choose an issue type when you don't want to?

Yes, usually, I don't want a issue type

(Issues created using templates on the web also seem to have no issue type)
Yeh fair enough @BagToad you did the work here, are we missing something in being able to avoid selecting a type?

@williammartin I think this is just an oversight. We should have a way to say you don't want a type interactively.

There's some related work going on in https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/13899 that I haven't had a chance to review again.

> We should have a way to say you don't want a type interactively.

Using config/option seems to bring a lot of trouble. Is there any harm in adding a `[None]` item?

> 12\. > We should have a way to say you don't want a type interactively.
>          
>          
>          Using config/option seems to bring a lot of trouble. Is there any harm in adding a `[None]` item?

Sorry for the confusion - I didn't mean to suggest a config option. I think your suggestion to add some `None` value to the options is the correction one 👍

I find this change also surprising: specifically the web allows me to create an issue without a "type" but the cli forces me to choose one.

What I expect is different from the OP: I'd expect the selection of "type" to move to the same place "labels" are i.e under *optional* metadata to add once the issue is created.

I do not think it's worth creating a different issue to describe this but I'm happy to if it makes things more clear.

comments.body:
### JSON format v2

Things to keep in mind / ideas:

- We could potentially include the full command line, in order to repeat a benchmark in an easy way
- For "matrix" runs, do we keep the flat structure or should we build something that represents the structure more cleanly?

> Additional performance metrics

How about supporting only two modes to begin with: `default` and `extended` modes. Default mode would collect the current duration metrics. Extended mode would include additional metrics from https://github.com/andrewrk/poop to begin with, which is 6 additional metrics.

This would allow supporting multiple metrics with *minimal implementation effort*, without blocking implementation of the other features, such as JSON support for all metric data, ability to select individual metrics from CLI, changing wording from fastest etc.

For the sole purpose of supporting multiple metrics with default vs. extended flags in the text output, if you agree this is viable, do you think we need https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine/pull/790 as a prerequisite?

Not sure if this is in scope for what was described, but I have a use case where I want to benchmark the decoding tokens/sec for local LLM API calls.

llama-server exposes these as fields in the returned JSON, so it would suffice to just parse using JQ and return the numeric value from there.

It would be nice if hyperfine allowed measuring arbitrary results of commands like this. One approach that comes to mind is:
* Optional wrapper command (passed in with the benchmarked command on the command line) that spawns the benchmarked command, measuring whatever metrics (e.g. memory usage) of the benchmarked command, or processing its output if necessary. Then the wrapper command returns a JSON key-value mapping of metrics -> value. Hyperfine then aggregates the JSON mapping emitted from the wrapper over each run.

Theoretically, the advanced metrics you mentioned (memory, CPU instructions, etc) can hook into this abstraction. It can be a bespoke util that wraps and measures these key metrics. It can be kept separate from the core engine (but for ease of use command-line flags like `--memory`, etc. can be added, which basically just activate "wrapper mode" with the first-party wrapper if present.)

A lot of things have happened now: additional metrics ([#983](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine/pull/983)), JSON schema v2 ([#790](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine/pull/790)), direct execution by default ([#982](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine/pull/982)), and the new terminal output, --metrics selection, and first-command reference ([#986](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine/pull/986))

What's still missing:

- baselines (Saved benchmarks for later comparison). The new JSON format and the new terminal output format should make this easily possible now, though.
- Interleaved benchmark execution: I haven't started working on this, but I'm not sure anymore if it should block 2.0
